results.caption: Rømø 🇩🇰 and Sylt 🇩🇪 Nude Beaches Rømø in Denmark and Sylt in Germany are two of northern Europe's most talked about clothing-optional islands, sitting just off the coast in the Wadden Sea and linked by a roughly 40-minute ferry ride. On Rømø, Sønderby Strand is a massive drive-on beach where you can park your car right on the sand, and because beach nudity is legal everywhere in Denmark, people just get naked with no designated zones or signage needed. Sylt plays by different rules: clothing-optional beaches there are signposted and organized, and Buhne 16, Germany's oldest nude beach and official since 1920, splits into a textile section, a clothing-optional stretch, and a zone where nudity is the rule, not the exception.   If Buhne 16 feels a little too busy (that beach bar pulls in plenty of textile visitors too), head north to List's official nude beach instead. It has its own parking area, a bus stop sign that tells you exactly what kind of beach you're walking to, and a quieter, fully nude stretch of sand with Strandkörbe dotted along it, just like at Buhne 16. Whether you want total freedom on Rømø's flat sand or Sylt's clearly marked zones, both islands make for an easy clothing-optional trip, especially since one short ferry ride connects them. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #germany #fkk #fkkstrand #sylt #romo #buhne16

North-West Germany FKK Nude Beaches (Wadden Sea Coast) North-west Germany's Wadden Sea coast is home to five clothing-optional beaches: Hooksiel, Cappel-Neufeld, Cuxhaven, Sankt Peter-Ording, and Holmer Siel on the Nordstrand peninsula, each with a completely different look and feel. What ties them together is the tide: at low tide, the water pulls back for miles across the Wadden Sea, leaving mudflats behind every single one, even though one has white sand, another is a grass field next to grazing sheep, and one has no sand at all. Hooksiel and Cuxhaven have been nude-friendly since the 1960s and 70s, but the real showstopper is Sankt Peter-Ording, a massive sandbar where the nude section sits right at the beach entrance, not hidden at some far end.   Each beach has its own quirks. Hooksiel gives you three and a half kilometres of white sand, rentable Strandkörbe beach baskets, a lifeguard, and a kiosk with toilets and showers, though the campsite's own FKK area there switches to textile after the 2026 season while the beach itself stays nude. Cuxhaven's FKK section is small, calm, and best for swimming at high tide. Sankt Peter-Ording charges a four-euro visitor tax but rewards you with one continuous stretch running from nude beach to dog beach to textile beach. Cappel-Neufeld trades sand for mudflats and a fenced sunbathing field, while Holmer Siel skips sand entirely for a grassy, sheep-grazed patch by the water. There's a naturist beach worth the trip wherever you land on this coast. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #germany

DON'T MISS These 5 French Naturist Resorts with a nude pool and beach. Sérignan Plage Nature, La Chiappa, Euronat, Arnaoutchot, and La Jenny are five clothing-optional resorts in France, each with its own nude beach and swimming pool on site, so you're never stuck choosing between the sea and the pool. One is on the Mediterranean coast, one is in Corsica, and three are on the Atlantic coast, where the beaches stretch for kilometers instead of meters. Sérignan Plage Nature is one of only two 5-star naturist resorts in France, with a supervised 500-meter sandy beach and a Roman-style balneo full of pools and jacuzzis. Over in Corsica, La Chiappa has two calm, sheltered beaches plus a heated and an unheated pool to pick from. On the Atlantic side, Euronat is the biggest naturist resort in this lineup, 335 hectares of pine forest backing onto 1.5 kilometers of nude coastline with old WWII bunkers scattered along the sand, and four pools including one built for kids and a tropical pool for relaxing. Arnaoutchot has a kilometer-long, west-facing beach for proper sunset swims, several pools, a quiet wellness area with jacuzzis, and new water slides opening in 2026. Last up is La Jenny near Bordeaux, a chalets-only resort with a 1,000-square-meter pool area split into four pools. Between them these five naturist resorts cover both of France's coastlines for anyone planning a clothing-optional beach holiday. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #france #euronat #arnaoutchot #lajenny #serignanplage #lachiappa

Corsica or Sardinia: Which is the Best Nude Island for You Sardinia and Corsica sit just 17 kilometres apart, and both are outstanding clothing-optional destinations in the Mediterranean, but they deliver completely different kinds of naturist holiday. Sardinia is all about wild, undeveloped nude beaches: Piscinas on the west coast is often called the biggest nude beach in Europe, with towering dunes and fine quartz sand, while Monti Russu in the north made Italy's list of ten most beautiful beaches and comes fully signposted as a nude beach. Corsica, a 50-minute ferry away, takes the opposite approach with a cluster of naturist resorts and campsites instead of scattered wild spots.   If you want structure over improvisation, Corsica delivers it. Bagheera has one of the Mediterranean's most beautiful nude beaches running for kilometres, Riva Bella offers a thalasso wellness centre, La Chiappa packs in a dive centre and horse ranch, and U Furu is a mountain campsite with a naked hiking trail along a river. Corsica also has its own nude beaches along the south coast and near the capital. Sardinia rewards naturists who like finding their own spot; Corsica suits those who want a resort base with activities built in. Combine both islands for the full clothes-free Mediterranean experience. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #italy #sardinia #france #corsica

The Nude Beaches of South Landes (🇫🇷 France) The south Landes coast in southwest France has six nude beaches spread across roughly 70 to 100 kilometres of Atlantic coastline, running from Plage d'Ondres near Biarritz north to Arnaoutchot near Vieux-Boucau. Outside the lifeguarded flags, nudity is broadly accepted on Landes beaches, and this stretch includes the department's only two officially recognized nude beaches: Plage des Culs-Nus in Hossegor and the beach behind the Arnaoutchot naturist resort. Every beach shares the same golden sand and dune backdrop, but each has its own personality, from a pink-painted bunker at Plage des Casernes to hand-carved shell art marking the nude section at Plage des Sablères.   Expect wide, uncrowded sand even in high season, wild Atlantic surf that draws serious surfers to Casernes and Culs-Nus, and pine-forest access roads that dead-end straight at the dunes. Ondres and Sablères sit near lively beach towns with bars and shops, while Casernes and Messanges North stay quiet and remote. Arnaoutchot flips the script entirely: naked is the norm, not the exception, thanks to the resort right behind the beach. If you're a longtime naturist scouting new coastline or planning your first clothing-optional beach trip in France, this guide covers what each Landes nude beach looks like, how to find the unofficial zones, and what makes each one worth the stop. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #france #arna #arnaoutchot

Sardinia vs Sicily: Best Nude Beaches Sardinia and Sicily both have real nude beaches, but they handle it in opposite ways. Sardinia has six officially recognised clothing-optional beaches, more than any other Italian region, spread across nearly 1,900 kilometres of coast, from the seven-kilometre dune-backed nude beach at Piscinas (named among National Geographic's 20 most beautiful beaches in the world) to the calm, signposted bay at Baia delle Ninfe near Alghero. Sicily takes the opposite approach: almost none of its 1,500 kilometres of coastline is officially marked, and most of its nude beaches are wild stretches inside nature reserves that you find by walking until you spot other naked people.   If you want everything signposted and easy, Sardinia delivers, with clear nude-section markers at Feraxi and Spiaggia Monti Russu (one of Italy's ten most beautiful beaches) plus quieter coves like Porto sa Ruxi and Cala di Volpe reached by short coastal trails. Sicily rewards more effort, with standout wild beaches inside the Vendicari and Torre Salsa reserves, at Capo Feto near Mazara del Vallo, and near Taormina, though a few spots like Bulala and Balestrate are worth skipping due to litter. Sardinia's swimming season really starts in late May, while Sicily's southern position keeps the water warmer through the shoulder seasons. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #italy #sardinia #sicily

Never Wear Clothes Again at These Resorts A clothes-free resort, also called a naturist resort or nudist resort, is a private, gated holiday spot where clothing is optional instead of required, with the same pools, restaurants, and beaches as any resort, just without the swimwear. The biggest difference from a public clothing optional beach is privacy: everyone inside the gate is a guest, which makes even a basic naturist resort feel more relaxed than the best beach spot.   You don't have to go clothes-free every second either. People cover up when it gets chilly, and nobody rushes first-timers. Every naturist resort runs on the same simple etiquette: always sit on a towel, never photograph other guests, and don't stare. Going without is usually expected in the pool or spa and more optional in the restaurant, depending on the resort. These places range from simple campsites to hotel-style properties with a spa and pool bar, up to entire naturist villages like Vera Playa in Spain. Booking works exactly like any other holiday, through the resort's website, with prices starting around twenty euros a night at a campsite and running into the thousands for a clothing optional cruise. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals

The Nude Beaches of Puglia, Italy Puglia, in southern Italy, has over 800 kilometers of coastline with several nude beaches scattered along it, from Vignanotica under the white limestone cliffs of Gargano National Park to Torre Guaceto, a sandy beach inside a WWF nature reserve near Brindisi where naturists have gathered for over 25 years. Most nude beaches in Puglia are unofficial but long tolerated, with one big exception: Termitosa recently became an official nude beach, a first for the region. In this guide we visit seven clothing optional spots along the Puglia coast, including Le Conche with its FKK graffiti and natural rock pools, the small cove of Pozzo Vivo near Polignano a Mare, and Spiaggia d'Ayala near Campomarino with its calm, shallow sea. We also tell you which beach to skip. If you're planning a naturist trip to Puglia or looking for the best nude beaches in southern Italy, this one covers the full range, from wild pebble coves to long sandy stretches that look almost Caribbean. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #italy #puglia #apulia

5 Highlights of Domaine du Coq Rouge Naturist Resort Domaine du Coq Rouge is a 4-star naturist campsite in Collonges-la-Rouge, Corrèze, in southwest France, and these are our five highlights after staying there. Start with a morning skinny dip in the pool before anyone else is up. Claim one of the outdoor beds dotted around the grounds, a feature we haven't seen at any other naturist resort.    Take a nature walk through the green Corrèze countryside on the campsite. Join a communal dinner and actually get to know the other guests, which happens more easily here than at bigger resorts. And book one of the unique accommodations, from tipis and stilted huts to ecolodges and bubbles, because a standard mobile home would feel like a waste at this place. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #france

Domaine du Coq Rouge Naturist Campsite in France Domaine du Coq Rouge is a small, family-run naturist campsite in Collonges-la-Rouge, in the Corrèze region of southern France, with around forty pitches and under thirty rental accommodations set on a hillside above the Dordogne valley. What sets it apart is the accommodation: bubble domes for stargazing, wooden tipis, Maori and Inuit-style tents, eco-lodges, and cottages on stilts with valley-view terraces, all built into the landscape rather than lined up like a standard holiday park.   The bar and restaurant sit at the centre of it all, serving homemade food from local producers, with theme nights, live music and karaoke a couple of times a week. There's a heated pool with a paddling pool for kids, a free sauna, a fitness area, hiking trails to a small farm, and leatherwork and jewellery workshops. The Camino de Santiago passes a kilometre away, and the campsite sits right where the Corrèze, Lot and Dordogne meet, next to Collonges-la-Rouge itself, the red sandstone village that gave birth to the "Most Beautiful Villages of France" label. It's a slow, sociable naturist holiday rather than a big resort experience, and the small scale is exactly what makes it work. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #france

This is one of France's largest clothes-free resorts Arnaoutchot, or Arna as everyone calls it, is one of the biggest naturist resorts on France's Atlantic coast, spread across pine forest and dunes in the Landes with its own clothes-free beach on the Côte d'Argent. The whole domain is 100% naturist, from the pools and restaurants to the on-site shop, and it packs a water park, a proper wellness garden and a kilometre of wild Atlantic beach into one site. You can make it a busy family holiday or a quiet escape in the pines.   Accommodation runs from chalets, cottages and mobile homes to glamping tents, treehouses and traditional roulotte caravans, plus camping pitches that go from premium spots to near-wild ones deep in the trees. Families get playgrounds across the resort and 60-plus activities a season through the Arna Club. The water park has an indoor pool and several outdoor ones, with new slides opening in summer 2026, and the Bassins d'Arna adds a sauna, hammam, jacuzzis and balneotherapy. One tip: be on the beach for sunset, because the coast faces west and it's worth the wait.
